metadata.note: The Stony Clove and Catskill Mountain Railroad (Phoenicia - Kaaterskill Junction - Hunter, opened 1882) and the Kaaterskill Railroad (Kaaterskill Junction - Tannersville - Haines Falls - Laurel House - Kaaterskill, opened 1883): two 3 ft gauge Cornell/Coykendall feeders to the Ulster and Delaware in the Catskill resort district, Ulster and Greene counties, NY. Run as separate companies until the U&D took them over in 1893; standard-gauged 1898-99; New York Central from 1 Feb 1932; closed together, reported 22 Jan 1940. These features replace the four Stony Clove / Kaaterskill branch features formerly in ulster_delaware_railroad.geojson. Research report: research/branches/kaaterskill_railroad.txt.

metadata.operator_split: Split at 1893 (SC&CM / Kaaterskill RR -> Ulster and Delaware) and 1 Feb 1932 (U&D -> New York Central); each span is its own feature on identical geometry, in its operator's colour (Rule 4). The 1893 split rests on period advertising naming the roads separately, their own officers and the 1894 locomotive renumbering (medium confidence); see the research report's ownership_split. The 1898/99 gauge change is not an ownership change and is not split.

1881 service Phoenicia - Edgewood: announced for 5 Aug 1881, not confirmed run; not drawn.
1940: the reported 22 Jan 1940 suspension year is not drawn (see not_yet_sourced).
The 1882 Tannersville Junction - Kaaterskill House carriage connection: road, not rail; not drawn.
No freight-only or horsecar content existed to omit (abandoned together 1939-40; steam throughout).
metadata.existing_layer_note: Replaces ulster_delaware_railroad.geojson features stony-clove-catskill-mountain-phoenicia-hunter, -nyc, stony-clove-kaaterskill-branch-tannersville and -nyc (removed there 2026-10-18). Defects fixed: Phoenicia - Hunter never reached Hunter (it ran 2.1 km toward Tannersville instead) and the 2.6 mi Hunter stub was missing; a 2.9 km out-and-back spike at Edgewood; the Kaaterskill Branch duplicated Edgewood - Kaaterskill Junction (SC&CM track); the Kaaterskill RR leg was drawn from 1882 instead of 1883; 1882-1893 was coloured U&D instead of the SC&CM / Kaaterskill RR; Tannersville - Haines Falls - Laurel House - Kaaterskill (4.5 mi) was missing in every era; no feature-level geometry_quality; the old note's 'standard-gauge Kaaterskill Railroad' (it was 3 ft until 1899).
not_yet_sourced: All headways and the 22 km/h speed: estimates; no timetable of any era was read.

End year: drawn to 1939. Every station is reported 'closed 22 Jan 1940' (Kingston Daily Freeman 22 Jan 1940, 'Mountain Branches Allowed to Suspend', via Wikipedia) - a headline about ICC permission. Whether trains ran into January 1940 or the last ran at the end of the 1939 season is unestablished; the Kingston Daily Freeman (fultonhistory / nyshistoricnewspapers) would settle it. Kaaterskill was summer-only by then, making a January train there doubtful.
NYC-era (1932-1939) passenger service rests on secondary sources only; no 1930s NYC timetable seen.

U&D takeover: 1893 (UDRRHS, second-hand; '4 June 1893' in the old layer unsourced) vs 1892 (Wikipedia U&D) vs 'incorporated in 1899' (Wikipedia Hunter station). Poor's Manual or the NY Railroad Commissioners' reports would settle it.
Hunter opening day: 24 Jun 1882 (Poor 1886 via Wikipedia) vs 29 Aug 1882 (UDRRHS, second-hand). Year 1882 either way.
Standard-gauging: SC&CM 1898 (UDRRHS) vs 1899 (Wikipedia Phoenicia / NRHP). No effect on drawn years.

Geometry: the Phoenicia junction with the U&D main and the Hunter terminal approach (0.78 and 0.79 mi) are unmapped in OSM and drawn straight; the exact Kaaterskill station site relative to the OSM way end is not pinned by a source.

segments.note: 3 ft gauge steam feeder to the Ulster and Delaware, from Phoenicia (U&D main line MP 27.5; Ramsey car-transfer from 1882) up Stony Clove via Chichester, Lanesville and Edgewood, through Stony Clove Notch to Kaaterskill Junction (called Tannersville Junction at first) and on to Hunter. Organized January 1881 under Thomas Cornell / Samuel D. Coykendall, with its own president and locomotives. Trains to Edgewood were announced for 5 Aug 1881 (New-York Tribune 29/30 Jul 1881) but no report that they ran in 1881 was found, so 1881 is not drawn. Open to Tannersville Junction by 24-26 Jun 1882 ('just completed', NYTR); in 1882 hotel passengers left the train there for a six-mile carriage ride to Tannersville and the Kaaterskill House - there was no rail east of the junction until the Kaaterskill Railroad opened in June 1883. Hunter's opening day conflicts: 24 Jun 1882 (Poor's Manual 1886 via Wikipedia) vs a mile short of Hunter on 24 Jun and Hunter itself on 29 Aug 1882 (UDRRHS, second-hand); 1882 either way. Through 1883-1889 travel advertising names the 'Stony Clove and Catskill Mountain' as a road separate from the U&D. Steam from opening; no animal traction. Headway is an estimate (summer resort traffic; no timetable seen).
sources: Segment-level: 1882 start from the New-York Tribune of 24 and 26 Jun 1882 (Hotel Kaaterskill ad; 'just completed, to Tannersville Junction'); Hunter 1882 from Wikipedia's Hunter station article citing Poor's Manual 1886, and UDRRHS (second-hand search summary, not read directly); separate operation 1881-1889 from NYTR items and ads; 1893 end = U&D takeover per UDRRHS (second-hand; conflicts: Wikipedia U&D '1892'). Headway NOT sourced - estimate.

segments.note: New York Central from 1 Feb 1932. Most intermediate stops became flagstops; Hunter, the busiest branch station, was one of two (with Tannersville) the NYC kept as an agency (agent eliminated 21 Feb 1940). End drawn at 1939: every branch station is reported 'closed 22 Jan 1940' (Wikipedia station articles, citing the Kingston Daily Freeman of 22 Jan 1940, 'Mountain Branches Allowed to Suspend', and the 1940 ICC Finance Reports), after ICC Finance Docket 12429 (filed 2 Jun 1939) for abandonment Phoenicia - Kaaterskill. That headline reports PERMISSION to suspend; whether winter trains actually ran into January 1940, or the last train ran at the end of the 1939 season, is not established, so 1940 is not drawn. Freight was abandoned with the passengers (scrapped 1940) - no freight-only afterlife. NYC-era service rests on secondary sources only (no 1930s timetable seen). Headway is an estimate.
sources: Segment-level: 1932 start from Wikipedia's U&D article; end from Wikipedia station articles (Hunter, Kaaterskill Junction) citing the Kingston Daily Freeman of 22 Jan 1940 and the 1940 ICC Finance Reports, and ICC Finance Docket 12429 (filed 2 Jun 1939) as quoted by abandonedrails.com - all secondary; the decision text and the newspaper were not read. Headway NOT sourced - estimate.

segments.note: 3 ft gauge mountain-top resort line from Kaaterskill Junction (end of the Stony Clove and Catskill Mountain) via Tannersville, Haines Corners (Haines Falls) and Laurel House to Kaaterskill station on South Lake, for the Hotel Kaaterskill and the Catskill Mountain House. Company established 25 Nov 1882; 'opened yesterday for business' (Daily Republican, Wilmington, 26 Jun 1883) - i.e. 25 Jun 1883, giving an all-rail route from Rondout to the mountain top. In 1882 there was no rail east of the junction: passengers left the Stony Clove train at Tannersville Junction for a six-mile carriage ride to the hotels (NYTR 26 Jun 1882). Advertised under its own name with its own General Passenger Agent (F. B. Hibbard, NYTR 6 Jul 1883) and held its own locomotives until the 1894 U&D renumbering; traffic officers shared with the U&D by 1890. Steam from opening; no animal traction. Headway is an estimate (summer season; no timetable seen).
sources: Segment-level: 1883 start from the Daily Republican (Wilmington) of 26 Jun 1883 p1, the Evening Star of 22 May 1883 and the New-York Tribune of 6 Jul 1883 ad; 1882 carriage connection from NYTR 26 Jun 1882; 1893 end = U&D takeover per UDRRHS (second-hand search summary; conflicts: Wikipedia U&D '1892'). Headway NOT sourced - estimate.

properties.geometry_quality: Traced from OpenStreetMap: 7.73 mi drawn against 7.3 mi documented (Fowler: Kaaterskill Junction MP 11.8 - Kaaterskill 19.1), 6% long. Per-station check (miles from the junction): Tannersville 2.80 (Fowler 2.8), Haines Falls station building (OSM 'Haines Falls Train Station') 5.23 (5.2), Laurel House Road / Kaaterskill Falls 6.67 (Laurel House 6.7). Fowler's 7.3 falls at about -74.050, 42.197 on South Lake; the drawn line runs on 0.4 mi beyond it to the north-eastern end of the OSM way named 'Kaaterskill Branch' (old_railway_operator=NYC) near the North-South Lake campground - taken to be terminal station/yard track, not the omitted Kaaterskill - Otis Summit connection, which lay to the south-east (this end heads away from Otis Summit); the excess is the whole of the difference from the documented mileage. Chained in order from OSM ways: the Tannersville grade (way 75965464 east of the junction), the Huckleberry Rail Trail, ways named 'Kaaterskill Branch', and the Kaaterskill Rail Trail, all old_railway_operator=NYC or named for the grade. The parallel Catskill and Tannersville Railroad grade (OSM ways 47062176, 1079507328, 1340750854, 1418309791), 0.3-0.5 km north between Tannersville and Haines Falls and alongside near Laurel House, was deliberately NOT used. APPROXIMATED, straight-line legs (1.27 mi in all): Tannersville - Haines Falls 490 m (0.30 mi) and 151 m (0.09 mi); at Haines Falls 548 m (0.34 mi); Laurel House - Kaaterskill 300 m (0.19 mi) and 277 m (0.17 mi); west of Tannersville 231 m (0.14 mi); approaching Haines Falls 41 m (0.03 mi). Simplified Douglas-Peucker 8 m + trim_reversals (0.01 mi lost). ALIGNMENT: the 1883-1899 narrow-gauge years are drawn on the surviving standard-gauge grade; no realignment at the 1899 gauge change is recorded in the sources checked.

segments.note: New York Central from 1 Feb 1932. Kaaterskill became a flagstop except in summer and Haines Falls summer-only, but both stayed on the line - no earlier cut-back of the Kaaterskill end was found; Tannersville stayed an agency. End drawn at 1939: every branch station is reported 'closed 22 Jan 1940' (Wikipedia station articles, citing the Kingston Daily Freeman of 22 Jan 1940, 'Mountain Branches Allowed to Suspend', and the 1940 ICC Finance Reports), after ICC Finance Docket 12429 (filed 2 Jun 1939) for abandonment Phoenicia - Kaaterskill. That headline reports PERMISSION to suspend; whether winter trains actually ran into January 1940, or the last train ran at the end of the 1939 season, is not established, so 1940 is not drawn. Freight was abandoned with the passengers (scrapped 1940) - no freight-only afterlife. NYC-era service rests on secondary sources only (no 1930s timetable seen). Headway is an estimate.
sources: Segment-level: 1932 start from Wikipedia's U&D article; flagstop/summer-only status and the 22 Jan 1940 closure from Wikipedia station articles (Kaaterskill, Haines Falls) citing the Kingston Daily Freeman of 22 Jan 1940 and the 1940 ICC Finance Reports; ICC Finance Docket 12429 as quoted by abandonedrails.com - all secondary. Headway NOT sourced - estimate.
